source.title: Measuring Memory and Generalization as Separable Geometric Channels: The Topo^2 Framework
source.authors: Zhang Zhang; Ming Liu; Qing Wang

record.file_problem: None; the complete paper text is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses geometric measurements and label-noise interventions to examine how memorization and generalization relate, but does not test the specific versioned claims' stated setups and measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on flipped-label memorization and validation accuracy, relevant to the broad topic. It does not test random-label held-out accuracy, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected networks, optimizer or batch-size comparisons, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or example removal as specified in the versions. Cited prior-work results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study measures memorization of a flipped-label subset and clean validation accuracy, plus geometric readouts and interventions. It does not test any stated version: V1 requires the random-label versus natural-label training comparison; V8 requires influence-selected example removal with a random-removal control. Its other comparisons measure different quantities from V2–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors present Topo2 as a framework for measuring and causally manipulating clean generalization and flipped-label memory through geometric readouts and FM0-based interventions. Their flagship quantitative claim is a memorization-cost law with coefficient near 0.38 at a reference capacity, explicitly dependent on capacity. They acknowledge that cross-channel topology is not an independent generalization predictor and that evidence strength varies across settings.
record.recipe_differences: Studies label-noise training interventions and topological measurements; the versions specify other training comparisons, architectures, regularizers, and sharpness or example-removal measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Training duration and intermediate evaluation cadence alter H1within; reported effects also vary by dataset, noise rate, protocol, and seed.

fits_no_version.finding: The corrected CIFAR-10 noisy-label run reaches validation accuracy 0.558; CONT broadly reaches mem_noisy≈0.999. The SVHN trajectory reaches mem_noisy=1.0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks trained on partially corrupted labels can memorize flipped labels while retaining clean-data generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: FM0 reports validation accuracy above 0.91 on CIFAR-10 and 0.96 on SVHN with approximately zero flipped-label memory.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suppressing loss on known corrupted labels can preserve high clean validation accuracy without fitting those corrupted labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Clean-only continuation reduces flipped-label memory from 0.999 to 0.11 while validation accuracy rises from 0.630 to 0.919.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continued training on clean examples can reduce corrupted-label memorization and recover validation accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: The clean-silenced condition has validation accuracy 0.04 versus 0.92 for the FM0 substrate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this overlay experiment, retaining clean training signal is necessary to preserve clean validation performance.

record.problems: Evidence is for selected label-noise settings, not the versioned random-label experiments. Several reported summaries have no uncertainty; the SVHN single-seed trajectory and some other cells are explicitly identified as single-seed. The supplied text does not report code availability.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant intervention results were extracted: most paper results concern topological channel behavior, pipeline validation, training determinism, or the fitted memorization-cost law, rather than a behavior named in the versions. Cited prior-work findings were excluded.

untested.parts: Matched architecture and training-recipe comparisons on fully random versus natural labels, including training fit and held-out accuracy under both label conditions.
Test error across widths beyond zero training error. The reported width sweep measures a memorization-cost coefficient and does not establish interpolation thresholds or test-error trends.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity or convolutional initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under specified tuning budgets and recovery recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce the penalty.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, underfitting, and joint dropout/weight-decay removal with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness versus generalization gaps and competing norm- or margin-based measures. Representation topology is a different measure.
Retraining after removing high-influence memorized examples versus equally many random examples, including dataset dependence.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the supplied claim versions; this does not dispute the reported intervention effects. Neither the topology results nor the noisy-label interventions justify verdicts on the versioned claims.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare networks trained on fixed random labels with natural-label training, or report held-out accuracy for random labels.
Does not test test error across widths beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks under the specified setups.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No large- versus small-batch comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Does not remove high-influence memorized examples and compare retrained test accuracy with random removals.

rows.subject: VGG×SVHN, η40, s42, CONV protocol
rows.operation_detail: Measured validation accuracy and fraction of flipped training samples predicted at their noisy label across training checkpoints.
rows.measure: Validation accuracy; mem_noisy (fraction of flipped training samples predicted at their noisy label).
rows.note: This is a late training checkpoint with saturated flipped-label memorization; the paper does not provide the corresponding validation accuracy in the table.
rows.check: Table 2 supports mem_noisy=1.0 and within=20 at epoch 300, but provides no corresponding validation accuracy. Within is a geometric ring count, not a validation-accuracy value.

rows.subject: ResNet×CIFAR-10, η40, CONT protocol
rows.operation_detail: Measured noisy-label memorization and validation accuracy after training with the corrected noisy-label script.
rows.note: The text identifies 0.558 as within the CONT range, but does not give a chance baseline or pair this value with a natural-label-only model.
rows.check: The corrected CIFAR-10 run uses η50, not η40. Its validation accuracy is 0.558. The mem_noisy≈0.999 value is a general CONT summary from the falsification ledger, rather than an explicitly paired measurement for this corrected run.

rows.subject: FM0, CIFAR-10
rows.operation_detail: Set zero loss on flipped samples from epoch 0.
rows.measure: Validation accuracy; memory on flipped samples
rows.note: The paper describes this as reaching the setting's generalization ceiling, but does not give a matched standard-training comparison here.
rows.check: The reported CIFAR-10 FM0 summary is supported, but omits a specific architecture and noise rate. Zeroing loss on known flipped samples does not test random-label fitting or influence-selected example removal.

rows.subject: FM0, SVHN
rows.operation_detail: Set zero loss on flipped samples from epoch 0.
rows.measure: Validation accuracy; memory on flipped samples
rows.note: The paper describes this as reaching the setting's generalization ceiling, but does not give a matched standard-training comparison here.
rows.check: The reported SVHN FM0 summary is supported, but omits a specific architecture and noise rate. It measures an oracle noise-masking intervention outside the stated versions.

rows.subject: CONT network, SVHN
rows.operation_detail: Continued training clean-only to strip memorized labels.
rows.note: The paper says accuracy recovers toward the FM0 ceiling; this intervention does not match the example-removal procedure in V8.
rows.check: The paired values are supported by Figure 5(c). Clean-only continuation removes training pressure from known flipped labels; it does not select examples by memorization influence, retrain from scratch, or compare with random removals as V8 requires.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10, memory with clean signal silenced
rows.operation_detail: Trained memory with the clean signal silenced (re-anchor experiment).
rows.note: The paper describes representation collapse; this is a different intervention from the versioned claims.
rows.check: Figure 5(b) supports validation accuracy 0.92 for FM0 and 0.04 with clean signal silenced, with an intermediate clean-present overlay at 0.53±0.004. These are condition comparisons, not an explicitly documented before-and-after trajectory. Validation accuracy alone does not establish that flipped-label memory collapsed.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
